title.narrative: Approach to the Concept and Practice of Heritage Authenticity in Africa

description.narrative: UNESCO World Heritage drives sustainable development by significantly impacting the identity and livelihoods of rich cultural heritage in Africa. However, the World Heritage List (WHL) faces the issue of representability, with only 108 sites in the Africa region, or 9 % of the total sites inscribed on the List. Additionally, 13 African sites out of 56 sites are on the List of World Heritage in Danger. These figures do not meet the targets of the 1994 Global Strategy for a Representative, Balanced and Credible World Heritage List and the objective of establishing the African World Heritage Fund (AWHF) in 2026. In fact, Africa still faces challenges in identifying its rich cultural and natural diversity of Outstanding Universal Value (OUV). There are many reasons why Africa faces challenges, including resources (human and financial), crises (sanitary, environmental and social) and academic (capacity development, training and expertise). For example, the understanding and application of World Heritage concepts such as OUV, which creates a gap between academic discourse and local practices, also hinder the implementation of the Convention, especially the identification and conservation practices. In line with World Heritage Committee decision 46 COM 11, this project aims to provide a platform for reflection in view of addressing this gap by enlarging, clarifying and identifying a new understanding of the concept of heritage authenticity in theory and practice in the African context. This reflection will contribute to UNESCO’s Global Strategy for a representative, balanced and credible WHL, and in particular, to set a foundation for implementing the Convention in Africa in view of supporting its representatively on the List and capacity development in Africa.
